land.text: the Alafin's Oyo, in the protectorate over Yorubaland that was 'incorporated into the new Southern Nigeria Protectorate in February 1906'

successors.note: The Southern Nigeria chain is carried by niger-coast-protectorate, as in lagos-colony's successors.

capitals.name: New Oyo (Ago d'Oyo, Oyo Atiba)
capitals.note: 'New Oyo (Ọ̀yọ́ Àtìbà), founded in the 1830s' as 'the capital of the remnant of the historic Oyo empire'; the Oyo Empire page says 'the capital was moved further south, to Ago d'Oyo'. The year of the move is page-silent; coordinates are the gazetteer's Oyo.

rulers.name: Atiba Atobatele
rulers.note: 'The Oba, otherwise called Atiba Atobatele, died in 1859.' The page gives no accession year; the entry starts at the state's start.

rulers.name: Adelu Alao Agunloye
rulers.note: 'His first son, Adelu Alao Agunloye, became the Alaafin after him and ruled from 1859 to 1876'.

rulers.name: Adeyemi I Alowolodu
rulers.note: Infobox '1876-1905: Adeyemi I Alowolodu'; 'the third Alaafin to rule in the present Oyo, who also died in 1905'. No page opened names the Alaafin of 1905-1906.

correction.text: the Alaafin's kingdom round New Oyo, the 'remnant of the historic Oyo empire'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: a 40 km disc round Oyo (the Alafin's town in lagos-colony ledger 5) and a 60 km disc round Ogbomosho (oyo-empire's successor entry). No page gives the Alaafin's territory after 1835: the Oyo Empire page has Oyo 'never regained its prominence', Ibadan charged with 'protecting the capital from the Ilorin' and the Ijaye with the western flank, and the Oyo, Nigeria page gives no area. The shape (about 15,200 km2) is a placeholder, against 150,000 km2 for the empire's peak ('By 1680, the Oyo Empire spanned over 150,000 square kilometers').

union.text: south of Oyo-Ile: 'the Oyo royal family fled southward to establish a new capital at Oyo Atiba (New Oyo)' (Old Oyo page); 'the capital moved south to Ago d'Oyo' (Oyo page)

region.text: New Oyo, 'the capital of the remnant of the historic Oyo empire', south of Old Oyo

ledger.note: 1835: the Alaafin's court re-forms at New Oyo. Ilorin 'eventually destroying the capital Oyo-Ile in 1835'; 'After the destruction of Oyo-Ile, the capital was moved further south, to Ago d'Oyo' (undated); the Oyo, Nigeria page has New Oyo founded 'in the 1830s'. 1835 is the year of the destruction, so the year of birth is a bridge, not a page date. Old Oyo had been 'deserted as a result of the Yoruba Civil Wars'.

3 February 1893: the Alaafin accepts British protection. 'Thus on 3 February 1893, Carter signed a treaty of protection with the Alafin of Oyo.' Mirror of lagos-colony ledger 5, which records Lagos as the protector.

28 February 1906: the protectorate over Oyo merges into Southern Nigeria. 'On that date the two territories were amalgamated' as 'the Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria' and the Lagos protectorate 'was incorporated into the new Southern Nigeria Protectorate in February 1906'; the page does not name Oyo, so the region is lagos-colony ledger 9's reading.

February 1906: New Oyo ends as a protected state. The Alaafin line continues (the Oyo Empire page: 'A remnant of the monarchy continues to exist as one of the traditional states of contemporary Nigeria') but the land is part of Southern Nigeria.

certainty.note: No page gives the Alaafin's boundary: the shape is two discs. The 1893 protection treaty and the 1906 amalgamation fix no frontier.

sources.title: Oyo Empire

sources.note: New Oyo (Ọ̀yọ́ Àtìbà) founded in the 1830s as the capital of the remnant of the Oyo empire; no year, no extent.

sources.title: Lagos Colony
sources.note: Carter's protection treaty with the Alafin of Oyo on 3 February 1893; amalgamation with Southern Nigeria on 28 February 1906.

notes: No Cliopatria row exists for New Oyo (Cliopatria's Oyo Empire row ends in 1835). Three pages opened (the Alaafin of Oyo page was silent on everything asked and is not listed). The state's life is page-thin: no page dates the move to Ago d'Oyo or gives the Alaafin's territory or authority over Ibadan, Ijaye, Ogbomoso or the Egba after 1835, so the 1835 start is a confidence-1 bridge and the shape a placeholder. Not settled: (1) Atiba's accession (1837 in other sources) is page-silent; (2) the Oyo Empire page is silent on the Kiriji War, the 1886 peace and the 1888 treaties, which a gap-filler should read in the Lagos Colony and Yoruba Wars articles; (3) the Alaafin of 1905-1906 is unnamed on the pages opened; (4) the dossier has no wars because none was opened that concerns New Oyo directly (the Ilorin raids of Atiba's day are undated on the pages); (5) the 40 km and 60 km discs overlap, and Ogbomosho's relation to the Alaafin is page-silent beyond the oyo-empire dossier's reading of 'south of Oyo-Ile'. After 1906 the Alaafin of Oyo is a traditional ruler inside Nigeria, which has its own dossier (federal-republic-of-nigeria).
